messages:
maya: quick heads-up — the int8 canary (raven-lite-int8) we rolled at 08:41 showed a jump in funcall JSON parse failures, ~3.4% -> 12.7% on the sampled traffic. opening thread to correlate logs and plan mitigations
ryan: yikes. is this mostly toolcall responses or general structured outputs?
maya: primarily toolcall responses. the client saw malformed JSON suffixes and truncated arrays. i grabbed a few samples.
chen: can you paste an anonymized sample?
maya: sure. raw model completion (trimmed):
```
{"tool":"search","args":[{"q":"latest qps"},{"page":1}]}
```
then the rest was `, "extra":` and cut — looks like suffix truncation mid-array
sasha: could be kv-cache or batching boundary causing mid-token cut. any correlation with seq len or batch size?
maya: spike coincides with higher batch windows (200–400ms) on the dedicated canary nodes. also more long-context requests in that 20m window.
qa-bot: telemetry snapshot attached: parse_error_rate:12.7%, median_completion_len:142, p95_latency:317ms, retry_invocations:0.8%
ryan: no retries? our retry budget is low for canary. we should try increasing soft retries for parse failures first.
chen: before changing retry logic, can we confirm it's model truncation vs postprocess truncation? i.e., is last token returned non-eos?
maya: in most samples final token is not <|end|>. it ends mid-token in many. shows last bytes don't decode to valid utf-8 sometimes.
sasha: that points to the runtime cutting response stream. what about the serving runtime logs? dev-bot, any deploys/ooms flagged in that window?
dev-bot: [deploy-bot] no config changes during window. GPU host 42 reported transient memory pressure at 08:44:12, recovered.
chen: memory pressure + batching could cause the runtime to drop in-flight tokens if kernel alloc fails. but why specific to int8?
maya: int8 canary had different kernel path and a smaller per-token buffer. we suspected that when we switched quant profile.
ryan: plan proposal: 1) pause canary for raven-lite-int8 2) roll back to raven-lite-fp16 variant on that cohort 3) run a diagnostic canary that forces single-request batching and dumps raw token stream to cloud storage for 15m 4) add temporary soft-retry on parse failures 5) add ndjson/len-prefixed snapshot tests in the eval harness
chen: agree. also add a small guard in postprocess: if final chunk does not parse as JSON, keep a short tail-buffer and wait up to 200ms for trailing tokens before trying to parse. that avoids spuriously cutting valid responses when there is slight stream lag.
sasha: that tail-buffer could trade latency — make it conditional only for canary/risky models.
maya: i'll implement the tail-buffer toggle and fast rollback. can someone own the snapshot harness change? we need to capture raw token-level stream + model config + kernel selection for each test sample.
ryan: i'll take snapshot harness. plan to add a `snapshot_id` header to canary requests and store the raw bytes in s3 with metadata: model, quant_profile, batch_size, kv_prefix, kernel_id.
chen: i'll triage runtime memory paths. maybe we need a guard that refuses new batches when available GPU free memory < X.
qa-bot: quick note: telemetry indicates these parse failures are concentrated on 3 templates that use multi-tool NDJSON outputs. single-tool calls are flat.
sasha: ok that suggests some interaction between longer outputs and NDJSON framing. we should also add a len-prefix mode in the toolcall contract for critical tool outputs.
maya: for immediate mitigation i'm pausing the int8 canary and routing to fp16. canary paused at 08:55. rolling back now.
dev-bot: [router] routing change applied — canary cohort switched to raven-lite-fp16 at 08:55:34
ryan: after rollback, parse error rate dropped back to baseline within one minute in the metrics. good signal.
chen: next steps: 1) reproduce locally with same quant kernels and artificial memory pressure 2) run single-request / no-batch diagnostic capture 3) run snapshot harness across 1k samples 4) implement tail-buffer for canary models 5) consider increasing retry budget for structured-toolcall failures from 1 to 3 short retries
sasha: add a follow-up to update the eval gating: require structured-output conformance < 1% on sampled NDJSON set before int8 canary promotion. also record p95 parse latency and p99 kvcache chop rate.
maya: noted. i'll file the PRs: runtime tail-buffer toggle, harness snapshot uploader, and the canary gating policy. putting links here when ready.
ryan: also add a quick smoke test to our CI: run 50 NDJSON toolcall samples through the quant kernels and assert valid JSON parse after a 200ms tail-window.
chen: thanks all — i'll post the triage run results in this thread after the local repro.
qa-bot: reminder: please tag `@oncall-infra` if you change the batch thresholds or memory guard so they can review capacity impact.
maya: tagging done. pinging infra.
ryan: temp checklist for the ticket: rollback done, snapshot harness owner = ryan, runtime patch owner = maya, local repro = chen, gating update = sasha.
sasha: i'll draft the gating policy language today.
maya: closing loop — feel free to DM if you want the raw capture samples. will update thread when PRs land. :thumbsup:
